content: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a graph-based index for approximate nearest-neighbour search. It trades a tiny amount of recall for enormous speed, letting vector search scale to millions of embeddings while keeping queries in the low milliseconds.

A cross-encoder reranker takes the query and a candidate document together and runs full attention across both, producing a far sharper relevance score than the bi-encoder used for retrieval. It is slow, so it only runs on the top-20 candidates to pick the best 5.

Lumina caches final answers in Redis keyed by a hash of the question. A repeated question returns the cached answer in well under a second, skipping embedding, retrieval, reranking, and generation entirely.
Lumina embeds text locally with the BAAI bge-small-en-v1.5 sentence-transformer, producing 384-dimensional normalised vectors. Running locally means there is no per-token API cost for embeddings.

Generation is delegated to a local LLM served by Ollama on the host GPU. Because the generator is written against the OpenAI-compatible API, switching to a cloud provider is a one-line configuration change.
